9.prefix_behaviour: On an empty score list the old line `metric_value = metric(scores)` crashed rather than returning anything — `accuracy()`'s body is `return total / float(len(scores))`, i.e. `0.0 / 0.0` → ZeroDivisionError — and `scorers_from_metric_dict` crashed one line later at `resolve_glob_metric_keys(metrics, scores[0])` with IndexError; `mean()` was already `np.mean([]).item()` → NaN.
9.postfix_behaviour: Empty input now short-circuits to `metric_value = float("Nan")` and `scorers_from_metric_dict` returns `[]`, so computing metrics over zero samples is legal and yields NaN instead of raising.
9.consumer: EvalResults.scores[].metrics[].value, read by the task display panel and written to the eval log — but pre-fix no consumer could ever observe the empty-input value, because the path raised (or was unreachable).
9.rationale: R2 fails on its face: the removed line `metric_value = metric(scores)` did not produce a healthy-looking number on empty input, it raised ZeroDivisionError (`total / float(len(scores))` in accuracy), and the sibling hunk's pre-existing `scores[0]` raised IndexError. A raise is explicitly excluded by R2. R1 fails independently: pre-fix the sole caller in run.py was guarded by `if len(completed_scores) > 0: results, reductions = eval_results(...)`, so the empty-measurement path was not reachable; this same commit adds the caller that passes `progress_results` while it is still empty (`update_metrics_display(len(progress_results), progress_results, ...)` right after `td.sample_complete(complete=0, ...)`). R3 is inverted: the fix replaces a crash with the sentinel `float("Nan")` to make zero-sample scoring permissible for the new real-time display, i.e. it loosens rather than fails closed. The hunk is also incidental — this is a 269-line, 8-file feature commit adding a live metric readout to the progress panel, and the results.py change is enabling plumbing for it, per its own changelog line "Allow scoring empty lists of samples".

9.prefix_behaviour: In `src/inspect_ai/_eval/task/results.py` the removed line was the unguarded `metric_value = metric(scores)` in `scorer_for_metrics`, plus an unguarded `resolved_metrics = resolve_glob_metric_keys(metrics, scores[0])` in `scorers_from_metric_dict`; both were only ever reached from `run.py` under `if len(completed_scores) > 0:`, so `scores` was never empty and no absent-measurement path existed.
9.postfix_behaviour: The same functions now short-circuit on empty input — `if len(scores) > 0: metric_value = metric(scores) else: metric_value = float("Nan")` and an early `return []` in `scorers_from_metric_dict` — so the newly-added real-time metric display can call `eval_results` with zero completed samples and render NaN.
9.consumer: The live task display metric line in `_display/core/panel.py` / `textual/widgets/tasks.py` — but that consumer is itself introduced by this same commit; pre-fix nothing consumed an empty-scores result.
9.rationale: This is feature enablement, not a silent-pass fix, and it fails on my lens plus a second requirement. R1: pre-fix `run.py` guarded the sole call site with `if len(completed_scores) > 0:` before invoking `eval_results`, and this very commit adds the new caller `update_metrics_display(len(progress_results), progress_results, ...)` placed immediately after `td.sample_complete(complete=0, total=len(samples))` with the comment "Update metrics to empty state". The empty-list path did not exist until this diff created it; the guarded quantity is the determinate setup-time condition "no samples have completed yet" in a brand-new display loop, not absent runtime measurement data on a pre-existing path. R2 independently fails: had the empty path been reachable, `accuracy`'s `return total / float(len(scores))` raises ZeroDivisionError and `scores[0]` raises IndexError, while `mean` uses `np.mean([])` which already returned nan — a raise or an already-distinct NaN, never a value indistinguishable from a healthy measurement. Only R3 holds, and R3 alone is not the rule. The commit subject "Show real-time metric" and the PR bullet "Allow scoring empty lists of samples" both describe adding a capability, and the hunk sits inside a 269-line UI change spanning eight display files.

12.prefix_behaviour: Pre-fix, when the server did NOT apply the errors filter (an older server ignoring the unknown `errors_only` query param), the CLI still produced a correctly filtered listing, because `_run_sample_errors` passed `select=lambda s: bool(s.get("error") or (s.get("retries") or 0) > 0)` and `_run_sample_listing` applied it unconditionally with `rows = [s for s in listing.rows if select(s)]`.
12.postfix_behaviour: The wire param is renamed to `filter=errors` and typed `filter: Literal["errors"] | None` on the route so an unrecognized value 422s, and the client-side `select` fallback is deleted (`rows = listing.rows`), with the docstring stating "The result is trusted as-filtered — no client-side fallback."
12.consumer: The operator running `inspect ctl sample errors` (the eval-set triage read) and any script consuming its `--json` `{as_of, samples}` envelope.
12.rationale: R2 plainly fails. The only "measurement did not happen" path the commit itself names is a server that ignores the filter param and returns the full listing — and pre-fix the CLI explicitly defended that path with a client-side filter (`select=lambda s: bool(s.get("error") or (s.get("retries") or 0) > 0)`), so the output the consumer saw was a genuinely correct errored/retried listing, not a healthy-looking fake. The pre-fix comment says so outright: "the `select` filter stays as the fallback for older servers". Nor was the value ever indistinguishable in the unparseable-value case: the pre-fix signature `errors_only: bool = False` already made FastAPI reject `errors_only=bogus` with 422, so the added 422 only closes a gap for a param NAME an old server would not know. The direction of the change also cuts against R3: the fix REMOVES the compensating fallback and accepts undefended version skew ("Skew with a server from an older install is not defended"), trading robustness for an extensible enum. This is an API rename/hardening refactor, not a silent-pass fix.
